newsitem.title: CANADA: Canfor says Nielssen departure amicable.
newsitem.headline: Canfor says Nielssen departure amicable.

text.p: Canfor Corp said on Friday that President and Chief Executive Arild Nielssen resigned on amicable terms but declined to discuss the reason.

Chairman Peter Bentley, who is taking on Nielssen's jobs until a successor is found, said his departure was not related to the forestry company's results. But he would not comment on speculation that the two had split over strategy.
"We had an amicable parting. Beyond that, I don't really wish to discuss it," he said in an interview.
"He is a very fine gentleman and I have enormous respect for him."
In an earlier interview, Nielssen declined to explain the reasons for his resignation. Analysts said the two men apparently had a falling out over strategy.
Bentley, a major shareholder and longtime chief of Canfor, has a reputation as a strong-willed and high-profile leader.
Bentley said the search for a replacement had already begun and he hoped to have a successor in place by the end of the year at the latest.
"From a personal standpoint, the sooner or better but it won't happen until we find the right person. The right person will take precedence over timing," he said.
Bentley, 67, stepped down as chief executive two years ago when Nielssen was named to the job.
